# Argus patches

Source: crates.io `gpui-pre-windows` 0.3.9, Zed revision `93d745668805029476e6d7fbb19652116fed51de`. The upstream Apache-2.0 license and package metadata are retained.

The package-local lockfile and unnormalized manifest are omitted; dependency resolution uses the workspace lockfile.

`src/directx_renderer.rs` batches per-draw constant parameters into reusable 64 KiB buffers. Devices supporting D3D11.1 constant-buffer offsets bind aligned ranges instead of repeatedly mapping a buffer for every draw. Unchanged batch layouts reuse the uploaded parameters. Device recreation clears these resources; drivers without offsetting retain the original binding path. Shaders, draw order, blending, antialiasing and sampling remain unchanged.

For bounds-only animations, the immutable prefix of the scene is copied as exact pixels from a cached texture. Batches at or after the first animated order still use the original rendering path. Complete paints, viewport changes and device recreation invalidate the cache; scenes with external surfaces use full rendering. Copying preserves output-merger state between batches. `ARGUS_GPUI_DISABLE_SCENE_CACHE` disables the pixel cache for controlled rendering comparisons.

Batches crossing the first animated draw order are split without reordering primitives. Retained frames restore the full animated masks, redraw the suffix and call `Present1` for that region; shrinking bars and translated images therefore erase their previous pixels. The dirty region is fully reconstructed on every frame, including intersections with earlier frames of the flip-sequential swap chain. Full draws and CPU readback still reconstruct the complete target; suffix shadows fall back to full presentation. See [DXGI incremental presentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddxgi/dxgi-1-2-presentation-improvements). Diagnostics include retained batches and dirty-region area.

The blend states for quads, shadows, underlines, sprites and path sprites accumulate coverage with "over" (`DestBlendAlpha = INV_SRC_ALPHA`) instead of adding the alphas. The premultiplied swap chain is composited by DWM over the window backdrop (Mica): with additive alpha a second translucent layer, or an antialiased edge on one, turned opaque and dropped the backdrop it should let through, so light-theme cards, controls, text and curves drawn on translucent surfaces came out grey and heavy. Opaque or single-layer content is unchanged.

Polychrome sprites marked `PolychromeSprite::AREA_FILTER` (images painted with `paint_image_subpixel`: chart curves rasterized at twice the device resolution and translated every frame) are sampled by area in `src/shaders.hlsl`: every texel under the pixel footprint (at least one texel, at most three per axis) is premultiplied and weighted by its overlap. Bilinear sampling of such a raster point-sampled at some subpixel positions, which stair-stepped steep edges as the curve scrolled, and mixed straight colours with the transparent black around a stroke, which darkened its edges. Other sprites keep bilinear sampling. The background-composing variant of the sprite shader accumulates coverage with "over", matching the sprite blend state; it used to add the alphas, so retained frames covered more of the backdrop under light-theme translucent cards than full paints did. The source is rounded to 8 bits before composing, which keeps composed frames within two code values of fully painted ones (mostly one).

`src/alpha_correction.hlsl` applies the system's grayscale enhanced contrast to light text (brightness 50% and above) too. Upstream (adapted from Windows Terminal) fades it out for text brighter than 75%, so light text on dark backgrounds rendered measurably thinner than the same font and size in the original WebView2 interface. Darker text replaces the DirectWrite contrast and gamma correction with Skia's mask gamma as Chromium applies it on Windows (gamma 1.2, contrast 0.2, text luminance quantised to 3 bits, background assumed to be its perceptual inverse); the DirectWrite correction drew dark text on light backgrounds 7–16% heavier than the original. The release shader build also reruns when the included file changes.

`src/direct_write.rs` lays out a variable font requested between its named instances at exactly that weight on the `wght` axis, as browsers do; previously Segoe UI Variable at 330 drew its Semilight (350) instance and at 500 its Semibold (600) instance, and a fallback font followed the instance's weight (Chinese at 500 became Microsoft YaHei UI Bold instead of Regular). Weights that have a named instance, and fonts without a weight axis, keep DirectWrite's own matching: axis values reach the fallback fonts too, and non-variable fonts matched by axis can pick a lighter face with simulated bold. Glyph runs on faces the text system did not create (fallback fonts, variable instances) are rasterized with the face DirectWrite laid out, instead of a face matched again by family and weight, which lost axis values and simulations.

`src/events.rs` minimizes from the caption button by posting `WM_SYSCOMMAND` / `SC_MINIMIZE`, as the system caption does, instead of calling `ShowWindowAsync`; the window subclass that fades the window (`window_motion.rs` in the application) sees the request. Without a subclass, `DefWindowProc` minimizes the window exactly as before.

The alignment and capability checks follow [VSSetConstantBuffers1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d11_1/nf-d3d11_1-id3d11devicecontext1-vssetconstantbuffers1) and [D3D11_FEATURE_DATA_D3D11_OPTIONS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d11/ns-d3d11-d3d11_feature_data_d3d11_options). `ARGUS_GPUI_DIAGNOSTICS` reports the selected capability for owned tests. Remove the patch when equivalent behavior is available upstream.
